1.1: Paul, a bondservant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, sent to build up the faith of God's people and get them to acknowledge the truth that leads to godliness,
1.2: With the hope of eternal life, which God, who can't lie, promised us before time even started,
1.3: But in His own time, He revealed His Word through preaching, which was entrusted to me by the command of God, our Savior.
1.4: To Titus, my true son in the faith we share: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior.
1.5: That's why I left you in Crete—to set things straight, fix what's lacking, and appoint elders in every city, just like I told you.
1.6: If a man is blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children who aren't out here wildin' or being rebellious,
1.7: A bishop gotta be blameless, a steward of God, not self-willed, quick-tempered, always drunk, violent, or greedy for money.
1.8: He should be hospitable, a lover of good stuff, sober-minded, fair, holy, self-controlled,
1.9: Holding on to the faithful word as he was taught, so that he can teach sound doctrine and correct those who go against it.
1.10: There's a lot of disrespectful people, people talking nonsense and deceiving others, especially those who say they're from the circumcision.
1.11: Their mouths need to be shut, they're messing up whole households, teaching things they shouldn't for the sake of dishonest gain.
1.12: One of them said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."
1.13: And that's real talk. So rebuke them sharply so they can get right in the faith.
1.14: Don't pay attention to Jewish fables and the rules men make up that go against the truth.
1.15: To the pure, all things are pure, but to those who are defiled and don't believe, nothing's pure. Even their mind and conscience are messed up.
1.16: They claim to know God, but their actions say otherwise—disobedient and disqualified for any good work.

2.1: But you? Speak the things that line up with sound doctrine:
2.2: Older men should be sober, respectful, self-controlled, strong in faith, in love, and in patience.
2.3: Older women too, should be respectful in how they carry themselves, not gossiping, not out here always drunk, but teaching good things—
2.4: They should be telling the younger women to love their husbands, love their kids,
2.5: Be wise, pure, keep the house in order, be good, and obedient to their husbands—so that the Word of God won't be disrespected.
2.6: Likewise, tell the young men to be sober-minded,
2.7: In everything, show yourself to be a role model of good works—let your teaching show integrity, respect, and uncorruptibility,
2.8: Your speech should be sound, so no one can talk bad about you. When your opponents see how you carry yourself, they'll be ashamed 'cause they won't have nothing evil to say about you.
2.9: Tell bondservants (workers) to be obedient to their bosses, to be pleasing in everything, not talking back,
2.10: Not stealing from them, but showing trustworthiness, so they can make the doctrine of God our Savior look good in everything.
2.11: The grace of God that brings salvation has shown up for all people,
2.12: Teaching us that, if we're gonna live right, we have to say no to ungodliness and worldly desires. We need to live self-controlled, righteous, and godly in this world,
2.13: Looking for the blessed hope—the glorious return of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
2.14: Who gave Himself for us, so He could redeem us from every sinful thing, and make us His special people, excited and ready to do good works.
2.15: Speak these things, encourage people, and correct them with all authority. Don't let anyone disrespect you.

3.1: Remind them to be subject to the rulers and authorities, obey them, and be ready for every good work,
3.2: Don't speak evil of nobody, be peaceful, gentle, and show humility to everyone.
3.3: We used to be just like them—foolish, disobedient, deceived, chasing after all kinds of lusts and pleasures, living in hate and envy, hating each other.
3.4: But when the kindness and love of God our Savior showed up,
3.5: He didn't save us because of anything we did right, but because of His mercy. He saved us through the washing of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Spirit,
3.6: Who He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
3.7: So that, being justified by His grace, we could become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
3.8: This is a true saying, and I want you to keep telling them that those who believe in God should be careful to keep doing good works. That's good and beneficial for everyone.
3.9: But stay away from foolish arguments, family trees, fights, and all that drama about the law—it's just useless.
3.10: Reject the person who's always causing division after you've tried to talk to them twice,
3.11: 'Cause you know they're messed up and sinning, self-condemned.
3.12: When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, be sure to come to me at Nicopolis, 'cause I decided to spend the winter there.
3.13: Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey quickly so they don't lack nothing.
3.14: And let our people also learn to do good works, help out with urgent needs, so they're not out here being useless.
3.15: Everyone who's with me sends their greetings. Greet the ones who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
